MCMC convergence diagnostics

Source: R/mcmc_diag.R
mcmc_diagnostics.Rd

Collects convergence diagnostics for scalar summaries of the chain, the Monte Carlo error of edge probabilities, agreement between chains and the samplers' acceptance rates in one table. Works with save_draws = FALSE: the traces and batch counts it uses are always kept.

Usage

mcmc_diagnostics(
  fit,
  c = NULL,
  scale = c("pcor", "precision"),
  rhat_max = 1.01,
  ess_min = 400,
  mcse_max = 0.05
)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list. Several chains are strongly recommended: R-hat from a single chain only compares its two halves.

c

Threshold for the trace of the number of differential edges \(|D| > c\) and for the Monte Carlo error of \(P(|D| > c)\). Default: the largest value of diff_deltas.

scale

Scale of \(D\): "pcor" (default) or "precision".

rhat_max, ess_min, mcse_max

Thresholds for the flags: R-hat above rhat_max (default 1.01), bulk or tail ESS below ess_min (default 400) and edge-probability Monte Carlo SE above mcse_max (default 0.05).

Value

An object of class "multiggm_diagnostics", a list with

scalars

Data frame with one row per scalar summary: quantity, mean, sd, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail, mcse_mean and flag.

edges

Data frame with one row per edge probability: quantity, max_mcse, median_mcse, n_mcse_above, max_chain_diff.

acceptance

Data frame of mean acceptance rates for the Metropolis-Hastings steps (G-Wishart and SSVS), with a flag outside (0.05, 0.95).

n_chains, n_iter, c, scale, thresholds

Settings.

Details

Scalar traces. For each chain the samplers record, at every post-burn-in iteration, the number of edges per group, the number of differential edges per pair of groups (structural, \(|D| > c\) and union for every c in diff_deltas) and the Gaussian log-likelihood of each group. These, together with \(\theta\) (G-Wishart, SSVS) or the edge-scale correlations \(R\) and global scales \(\tau\) (mGHS), are summarized by rank-normalized split R-hat and bulk and tail effective sample sizes (Vehtari et al. 2021), the same algorithm as the posterior package. A whole-graph summary such as the number of edges is a sensitive check: chains stuck in different parts of graph space disagree on it.

Edge probabilities. R-hat is not informative for single 0/1 edge indicators. Instead, edges reports the batch-means Monte Carlo SE of every edge probability used for selection (largest and median over edges, and how many exceed mcse_max), and, for several chains, the largest difference in an edge probability between any two chains. An edge whose probability is within a few Monte Carlo SEs of a selection cutoff is not reliably selected or rejected; run the chain longer.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. & Buerkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: an improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667-718.

See also

plot_trace(), plot_chain_agreement(), edge_probs()

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs", burnin = 200,
                     nsave = 200, nchains = 2, seed = 1, save_draws = FALSE)
mcmc_diagnostics(fit)
